reviews.text: I've been enjoying the demo for months and I'm happy with the full game now that it released. I'm looking forward to more content.

A solid game building off the improvised mechanics of Keystone, which I still play today. Play cards to send units, build structures, buff units or take explosive actions. Easy to pick up, but the more you look the more depth there is. Do you align your cards timing wise, but risk the opportunity cost? Do you build to be able to make a focused stratagem of your own, or do you ensure you have answers for an opponents strategy? The dev obviously has passion and dedication, their discord server is active, and they still update Keystone which was the mod that this is the stand alone game for. I'm glad to see they've been able to convert from modding to full game, that is not an easy measure by any means. They obviously have a ton of ideas, and an understanding of how part of the fun of any game is creating interesting combos and interactions. Plus it looks like they've avoided the trap of taking the easy path of slop, so massive props for them. They keep patches coming, and explain their thought process, so you can be sure this is a product and a person worth supporting. Music is a little repetitive, but for a first time dev its very reasonable, and its not an annoying repetitive. All in all, definitely recommend as its own game, and recommend more because the dev deserves support as well. Thank you standarddevguy.

Honestly a fun game, it's simple to pick up but is easy to lose track of time in. It's a deckbuilder with both a roguelike mode and a campaign mode. The game itself plays by playing cards that have various effects (Units, Structures and actions) Units will appear next turn (this turn if they have rush) and will move from your half of the screen to fight your opponent, structures appear instantly and have a variety of effects ranging from defensive structures, spawners or other kinds of benefits. Actions meanwhile take effect immediately and can either buff your units or damage/affect enemy units. The flow of the game begins with you picking your opening hand and either redrawing it or keeping it, then you will pick which of the two resources to gain; each turn you get to pick a resource so that you can play a card or more in your hand each turn letting you climb up to more expensive and powerful cards. Additionally a lot of the cards belong to particular subfactions which all tend to revolve around a shared gimmick for example one subfaction likes to keep cards in your hand if your opponent has more units than you when you play them which lets you play them every turn if your opponent is overwhelming you. Another subfaction likes to use number manipultion to become incredibly powerful for example adding +1 to all numbers on cards in your hand (aside from cost) or doubling the number of units on a card. All in all is the game perfect? No, but is it bad? Definitely not, This the first proper game that this dev has made and personally I think they've done a fantastic job at making it, I am certainly looking forward to future updates.

A unique card game where you impact the battlefield by deploying units, structures or use Action cards for all kinds of effects. The developer previously worked on a free Starcraft 2 arcade game called KeyStone that inspired the creation of a stand-alone title. Good game.

Launching the game on the last day of the steam sale without a launch discount is a bold strategy, but I hope it works out, as it does seem like the game is built for future expansion. It's a neat evolution from Keystone, which is a Starcraft 2 Custom map the dev previously made. I have hundreds of hours in Kestone and I have about 10 hours from the demo, but from the end of the demo I finished the story campaign in about 4 hours - the roguelike mode is definitely the main appeal here, and that's pretty good!

UPDATE at 10hr's: Yes game is still not fun, which sucks because this can be very very good. Very little deck control (adding removing) Cannot find cards that work together before dying. I have no idea how many waves or what's coming. Flaregate Network is a fun game with a lot of potential, but it can also be incredibly punishing at times. The storyline isn't anything groundbreaking, and many of its themes feel familiar, but it's intriguing enough to keep me invested and wanting to see what happens next. The gameplay is where the game shines. There's a satisfying challenge here, and I generally enjoy difficult games that require strategy and planning. That said, the difficulty can sometimes feel unfair rather than rewarding. One of the biggest issues is the lack of information provided to the player. Enemy intentions are often unclear, and unless I've missed it somewhere, there doesn't seem to be a turn counter or a clear way to anticipate what's coming next. When you're still learning the mechanics, this creates situations where defeat feels unavoidable rather than earned. I've also run into stages that seem impossible to complete with the cards and perks currently available. Whether this is a balance issue or simply a knowledge gap remains to be seen, but it can be frustrating when progression feels gated by factors outside the player's control. Another issue is that some cards don't appear to properly reflect additional stats, bonuses, or unit interactions. This makes it difficult to make informed strategic decisions and can lead to confusion about whether certain effects are working as intended. A major question I keep asking is: when do I unlock new content? The game's progression system could do a better job communicating upcoming rewards, unlocks, and milestones. Knowing what I'm working toward would make setbacks much easier to accept. One thing that surprised me is how little feels new compared to the demo. The demo was fantastic and offered a substantial amount of content, which set high expectations for the full release. So far, I haven't encountered enough new content to make the full version feel significantly different from what I already experienced during the demo. That doesn't mean there isn't more to discover, but the early impression is that the jump from demo to full game feels smaller than expected. The main reason I paid $15 for the game, was because of the demo. Despite these frustrations, I'm still playing because the core gameplay loop is genuinely fun. The challenge is engaging, the story is interesting enough to keep me invested, and the game clearly has a solid foundation. However, the difficulty can feel overly punishing, progression isn't communicated very well, some cards need clearer descriptions, and the full release currently doesn't seem to offer much beyond what was already available in the excellent demo. At $15, I don't regret the purchase, but I do hope future updates add more content, improve balance, and provide better information to players. Right now, Flaregate Network feels like a game with a lot of promise that's still missing a few pieces needed to fully realize its potential. Will this be another abandoned project? I don't know. Reading the discussion on steam, the dev seems engaged, but not very open to suggestions. Not all suggestions are good :-) Score: 6.5/10 — Fun and addictive, but occasionally frustrating and in need of additional content and quality-of-life improvements.

A vastly original take take on a card game, you play an RTS / Tug of War with cards. Roguelike mode is thoughtful and challenging in many unusual ways, e.g. the order in which you undertake missions matters, scouting ahead for rewards matters, NOT taking the strongest card sometimes is the correct choice as is NOT playing a card - knowing when to do what based on what is going on on the battlefield is key. Multiple mechanics, multiple ways to win the game. Highly recommend for any card roguelike fan.

I've been waiting for this to come out ever since I saw it on the Keystone loading screen. Having played through a couple more hours of the full game after having completed the Demo several times I really want to say thank you for making this come true. As for highlights, ever since keystone I've been a big fan of Structure decks, so my views are gonna be slightly biased, but I love love LOVE Director Keys (His name is a Halo reference right?) because he basically doubles my structure's output. Him combined with some scaling up on Destroyer Factories and it's absolutely awesome how many ships I can get out. All this to say, I really like this game and look forward to playing more of it.
Really excellent game. Very quick to pick up and lots of depth. Plays a bit like mechabellum but with card game mechanics.

I think the game is priced too high at $15 [for anyone interested in the rogue-like runs, not the campaign]. The core gameplay loop exists, but the content to justify going through a new run is...lacking. Once you have beaten it once, you'll likely have seen what possible options exist for another run---and it isn't all that enticing. Build variety is too small, the tech tree not all that engaging, and anything "cool" you think you could pull off is buried by forced taking of cards and only one use per card. The game would be much better if cards could recycle in the deck, you could remove cards from your deck, and you weren't forced to take a card. You could argue that this is what makes the game "good" and "challenging" (it's not that challenging), but it doesn't make the game more fun for me---it takes away from its potential. If the game's core structure stays the same, then more factions are needed to justify the cost and increase the hours I'd be willing to put into the game tinkering. I will say the game does exist outside of your typical roguelike deckbuilder---and that was refreshing, but not refreshing enough to keep going.

It's just bad. The story mode is billed as a learner experience, it is basically unplayable and outright hostile to a good game play experience. The rogue like mode is almost tolerable, but you are at the whim of RNG on card and ability draws between missions, which might as well be predetermined. This game was made by someone with no sense of fun or joy in their life, let alone any concept of game balance.

The core gameplay (the underlying card game) seems absolutely amazing, but the way you engage with it really doesnt do it justice. So while I feel like it could unironically easily be one of the best CCG's on the market, atm its just kinda meh unfortuantely. The two available game modes are Campaign and Campaign (someone needs a thesaurus), and the big problem with both is that theres not really any traditional deckbuilding, which would be ok as a secondary game mode but with so many fun cards and obvious builds, I hate that being able to build a fun deck is either time gated (story) or based on RNG (adventure). These deck building restrictions are a useless attempt to reinvent-the-wheel. If you dont want it to be a TCG, make it a Deckbuilder where you unlock entire sets of cards, such as "Human - Pirate" or "Human - Invention" which are both real sub categories in the game with thier own unique mechanics. Taking half the fun out of a card game is not clever or rewarding. The Story mode is WISOTT, Human only ATM it seems, and you do deckbuild a little but youre very much on rails for the most part and it opens up VERY slowly. Its reaching a lot higher over all than the writing can carry it, thats for sure. If the characters continued the GUNDAMN esque style (instead of what ever disgusting style it is) that is used for all the other non-character cards it would be perfect, because those other cards have really good art. Otherwise the writing is very amateurish and the pacing is incredibly drawn-out, those two things making it very very difficult to stick with the story. The other mode which should be called Adventure but instead is called "Standard Campaign" (*shrug*) is interesting. The combination of card game mechanics and its adaptation into a rougelike mode work really well together as something refreshingly different, though it would still be better if it used a more deckbuilder-like system instead of pure RNG it would hands down be better, or even if you at least could start with a custom deck that has at least some kind of basic synergy or theme. Not having any MP game mode seems pretty wild. I think it goes without saying that it definitely needs to have some kind of MP game mode added ASAP. Be it 3v3, 1v1, or prefereably both, every cool looking card art or interesting mechanic or wild synergy combo, its all wasted without PvP and if this were just some shovelware game it wouldnt matter, but the gameplay is there, the card art is there, the combo's and synergies are there, so its incredibly disapointing that they are locked away as they are, even outside of the lack of MP. The audio is very basic. I dont think anyone took its creation seriously, which is a shame as you can imagine instantly how much better the experience would be with some more detail and additions like unit barks on summon. Visually its a mixed bag unfortunately. The human forces have an interesting and distinct aesthetic that I feel like instantly fits into GUNDAM, to the point I wonder why there are no mech units, but the alien forces are a bit boring. Also it would look infinitely better if it were isometric rather than this classic Flash style of JPG's sliding around, and obviously even better if it were 3D, and the fact that at least with the human units being so good looking on the cards, makes this even more unfortunate that outside of the card art they look so horrible and are literally flat. Speaking of the other factions, while its hard to tell without getting your hands on these factions, they do seem to be mechanically interesting and seem like well balanced asymetrical factions that games have failed creating competently for 20+ years, but coming from SC i guess this game had a good role model in that regard. Thats the game as it is, as i see it. I can seriously see this game being massive, or maybe a sequel of it. Potentially the next DOTA level of success from a Blizzard custom map, but if they leave it as is it will just be a Red Solstice at best. Also I would love to see the game potentially leave its strictly space restricted theme so that ground vehicles, infantry and aircraft could be added to increase the depth of the game, be it in there being more room for interesting card designs or layering unit interactions, and another personal wishlist item is a grand strategy meta game mode. I have a personal fondness for the Battletech TCG, and feel like some similarities can be drawn between this game and that.

This game is honestly really something unique. While it might not be the strongest game in any given genre, it excels at mixing them into something not really seen before, combining deckbuilder, auto-battler, and RTS elements together quite well. I went in expecting something like Keystone (the dev's original card game auto-battler inside of starcraft 2) but it managed to twist the formula in a lot of ways that kept it engaging. There are some really creative cards in here that can lead to some crazy combos (might of the empire my beloved). But what I wasn't expecting at all was a really engaging story. The game is full of morally gray characters whose mistakes and attempts to fix those mistakes bring things from small scale scuffles into a galactic tragedy with a very smooth difficulty curve. While the AI isn't anything fancy during individual missions, they slowly introduce mechanics that challenge your playstyles in interesting ways during the meta-campaign and force you to adapt your strategies, and the "signature strategies" mechanic (cards you are guaranteed to start with) removes a lot of the opening hand RNG card games often struggle with and make the game a lot more strategic. You don't have to rebuild your deck to alter your strategy for each individual mission. The mission variety is genuinely great, especially the puzzle missions which make you really alter your strategies. But the game is good without the story too, and the rougelike mode is a perfect place to experiment with decks if you just want to have fun. Is the game perfect? No. It's slow paced, there is still a lot of RNG, and the music can be a bit repetitive (tho its not bad!) But is it enjoyable? Absolutely. As long as you have the patience to get through it's slow start. I'm in act 3 at time of writing and I'm genuinely hooked. My advice that I strongly encourage is to play the demo first, your save data carries over and you can finish the first act of the story. If it seems up your alley, get the full game, if it doesn't, save yourself 15$. A lot of the negative reviews seem to be from players who just didn't have the game click with them due to its weird mashup of genres when they were expecting more of one - but that's why you can try it out for free and decide for yourself it its your thing. This game isn't everyone's type, but it sure as heck is mine :)

Flaregate network is game whose gameplay originates from a Starcraft 2 arcade by the same creator. The game is advertised as rougelike, but the mechanics by which you actually play are quite different from nearly all other rougelikes on the market, and are in my opinion very fun once you get to know them better. The game, as of writing this review, consists of two main parts: - The campgain, which teaches the mechanics and goes over an alright story. From what I have seen heard should be maybe 12ish hours for new players. Currently consists only of one faction, final version should include 3. - The rougelike mode, this is the replayable experience and is quite fun in its own right, the structure of progression is similar to other rougelike games with winning the rougelike unlocking new difficulty level. From what I have played in final version, and before in demo, it is quite nice and if you enjoy other card rougelikes I think you may find this one refreshing and fun. Overall there are also some issues, mostly lacking some QoL features, but I have not experienced any bugs in the final release and can say that even if I mostly wanted to play the game for the rougelike, the campaign was also very enjoyable and I think this may be a more universal experience.

I finished the Story Campaign, and have done a few Roguelike runs as well. I'd give the game a B rating overall, but if you're like me and you love spaceships shooting at each other, you'll be happy with Flaregate Network. I'd describe the story as a cliche setting but with believable characters, and it entertained me the whole way through, and left me wishing for more. The roguelike mode isn't as compelling, due to the lack of narrative stakes. The card game itself is relatively straightforward, with relatively few "combos" or broken deck builds, though I do really like the "Signature Strategy" mechanic (which lets you guarantee cards in your opening hand) as well as the "Reserve" mechanic (which lets you remove cards from your deck) - especially with how they are adjustable from encounter to encounter, rather than being permanent choices. This helps variety within a single deck, though does have the knock-on effect of making decks somewhat similar across runs. A lot of the game hinges on exploiting the targeting priority of ship AI as well as timing your attacks, which isn't bad per-se but does feel a bit hollow after a few hours. I think I'm likely done with the game after ~14 hours, unless they add more content, but I enjoyed my time. Overall: I like it when spaceships shoot each other, and Flaregate Network gives me just enough control over that ship-shooting to keep me coming back, at least until the end of the campaign.

About 20 hours of content. Was worth the money. Nothing special. Being able to control deck bloat more would be nice to really have different builds/runs. Most of the runs I had to repeat were due to back deck drawing from unpreventable deck bloat I could easily see room for this game to expand with playing as the different races and continuing the story (like as the aliens defending against the humans)

Got to the second act and the drone swarm or whatever its called is just a complete joke in terms of balancing. Like, I had 0% chance of winning that fight even if I could play all my cards at once. Game needs work. Trying a second time, again act 2 is WILDLY imbalanced. Like some missions just feel like the developers have never once played a game in their lives with how completely hopeless these tier 5 or 6 missions feel. I should get to spawn a Titan, the strongest creature I can spawn, and it literally melt within half a second because the enemy gets to ♥♥♥♥ out SO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MANY enemies that they can rip through all of my units with mobs to spare. I should feel like I can actually win some of these. I feel like if every single card I had spawned double what it did, I still would not have even come close to winning a tier 6. The missile battery costing 3 and 1, and giving you A SINGLE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ volley of missiles is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ punch in the face. If you are going to make it give you only ONE volley, why the ♥♥♥♥ does it cost the same as a normal volley. Make it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ free, I just spent an assload to get this thing out, what is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ point of making it cost something as well. I literally only get the ONE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ volley. I haven't found a single "character" to remotely do anything useful. To make it even BETTER, they are so bad at balancing their fights, that the literal campaign, that has SET REWARDS for each fight, has a fight in its first few missions that you cannot win. I am literally 5 or so fights in. And there is a fight that the enemy can overwhelm you and you have no hope of winning. Its a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ joke. Skip this game until they actually take some time to make it more fun and balanced.

Played through the campaign and 3 level of roguelike as of 15/062026, had a great time! I liked the story. The campaign is great, the roguelike feels even better as it feels more "flexible" in terms of strategy with the upgrade, as well as more punishing as you can retry each mission like in the. You get experience fighting the different ships in the campaign, which is key to a good roguelike run. Eager to try cards from the other faction when they come out :) As for QoL, even when the game is at 3x, I would keep the animation that shows discarted card when you hand is full at the same speed as normal. as it goes so fast you can't see it. (My playtime doesn't match as I played offline a lot, I think I have around 6 more hours that aren't showed here.)
Leaving positive review with no real review rn cause the games' good enough to deserve it. Will update once I get through the story proper.
Wildly unbalanced and lacking content. Devs seem to have little to no idea what a CCG game is.

Disclaimer: I have played the previous Creator's Work on "Starcraft 2" called "Keystone Card Game" which was the inspiration for this game. Great things I enjoy: - Love the overall gameplay of combo things together. - Campaign is very straight forward on how to teach you things and progression. - It is fairly clear what is going on. - Great to add Fast-Forward feature. When combat is absent, this speeds up the game progression. [Comparison] I prefer the increased 10-hard hand-size versus 8. This also includes utility cards such as card-draw being better. Good Things: - For Campaign/Roguelike Card Removal via Reserve is nice. It makes it significantly less punishing to recruit/add a card early that has high-synergy with a playstyle but no immediate benefit for a deck. Later on, you can swap out other cards that are no longer needed. - Game works pretty similarly to everything I liked in Keystones. - I like that you can choose where you want to build a structure. It also enables you to manipulate the enemy forces this way to (placing it on them or away for delaying tactics). Things that I'd like to see: [Note: I have a lot of expectations, but that just goes to show how much I enjoyed the Starcraft 2 Keystone] - General Mode: Deckbuilding - Just standard game versus an AI where you can craft a deck of cards you currently have collected/received. - Cooperative Mode: Keystones is most known for its 3v3 mode. This game actually already has cooperative instances in the Campaign on a few select missions. - More sets of cards. Obviously this would be an expansion. (This includes the other races TBD). Things I'd like changed: - [Structure capacity / change] I've run into multiple issues where I've reached the capacity of structures. IMO, 7 isn't a lot when you have a large variety and you cannot replace them. I've had instances where I had to place early defensive turrets or resource generator structures, but then I wanted them removed so I can place down Production Structures. This is especially true if there is every a cooperative mode. The cooperative Campaign Missions show how this really hurts when your ally also puts down structures. - Starting Ship is insanely OP: Your starting ship honestly does an absurd amount of damage that rushing seems dumb. You always want to fight under your ship since it is the last priority. - Early Deck Size. The early deck-size feels WAY to small. The starting ship just attacks after 4 - 5 rounds at the start of the Campaign/Rogue-Like much to my dislike. It feels like I just need to "Hold off rushes" simulator. I think the ships attack-move can also be slowed down. - Unit-stack. All units have no collision with each other and can cause immense stacking and snowballing. AoE is designed to deal with this but the action cards just don't feel like they do enough. - Proactive Actions [Comparison]. They don't feel good enough. There aren't enough units, stats, or buffs to make them do enough. In Starcraft 2 Keystone, the diversity is significantly higher and there are many cases where your "Kill a Strong Unit" costing 2/1 in resources goes and kills something worth 5/3 or even 8/3 resources. The strongest unit your hitting in this case is worth 3/1 (And its damage is low? Even if its piercing, this damage needs to be increased as new "keywords" that effect unit stats are added. Similar to "Heroic" in Starcraft). I am also often surprised when Missile attacks just don't feel like they are accomplishing a ton. Similar effects in Keystone do significantly more damage, in cases where its 3v3 so there are significantly more units (less likely to stack, but units in this game stack only upon reaching a fight). Dislike/Please Fix: - Dusk Wings...? (Cloaked Human Fighter) feels absolutely broken. Cloak is extremely annoying to deal with. And this is especially true on the Human Faction cloaker unit as it deals High AoE Damage. A few of these units will deal with every single attack from the opponent as long as they are cloaked. - Map-Length and Insane Starts: The AI often has ludicrous starts. Since you can see your own card equivalent, the cards they send at what your resource count would be is often 50 - 100% more than what you would. Furthermore, the AI sometimes just starts with a large army that attacks you. If it wasn't for the fact that your Primary Ship isn't broken, it would feel impossible. I had multiple cases where turn 1 ramping to maximum resources (Tax card) somehow wasn't fast enough. It makes me think if you didn't get specific cards, how you would even possibly win. I've completed the Campaign, and completed 1 Roguelike adventure (few attempts too that didn't make it, some due to greed). The Roguelike feels weird in the sense that you don't upgrade your cards and all the cards feel kinda... vanilla? In a lot of Roguelikes, your starting deck/resource is absolutely terrible and you get additional cards/effects that are strictly better. Card Rewards feel way less important and sometimes feel outright like downgrades if they aren't good cards. Upgrade system is interesting but it doesn't feel like its massive powerspiking (I've only played a couple though). The starting bonus by far feels the strongest. I think the other options of taking "Repair" to your Primary Ship could be improved since skipping "increase maximum resource" feels like a losing cause. - Let me know if multiple runs of the Roguelike is very different as it did mention there are changes depending on how many wins you get. Overall: 7/10 I think Keystone is better but this is an indie game and its start. Most indie games with this start (from a previous game) usually have a rough start and get significantly better as they are further developed. I have high hopes for this game in the future. If a cooperative mode is added with any DLC, I will be purchasing them too. P.S. - I imagine that could make a cooperative Roguelike mode OR versus mode by copying decks from other players and giving them to the enemy AI similar to "The Bazaar" if there is a multiplayer-low player count issue.

This game has really good bones. i had been waiting for this since the moment i saw that the maker of Keystone was working on a full game. Overall good stuff in here. The standard campaign is great with just some oddities in the draw rate on some things. NOW. the issue. the story campaign will make you want to tear your hair out. most of it works great, however you will run into missions, bunches of them, where you just have to keep restarting the mission until you get the perfect hand because half your cards are useless and the AI is going to come at you hard and fast.

This is a neat game, it has some promise, but the card design, a few mechanics and especially the proposed challenge in front of you fails to celebrate anything exciting you do but only seems to underline any weakness in your deck and strategy, like when the game decides that structures are basically useless when you've aimed for a structure heavy strategy. The game in story mode attempts to show you that you can "choose your own strategy", by showing you cards that scales off tags like pirate, and soon after giving you a card that scales off having filled the board with structures. But you not only don't get enough pirate cards to make them worthwhile, aiming for a singular strategy is also immediately punished by the game in front of you, and the tools to refurbish your deck is severely lacking, you can't go back and repick cards that would help against the challenge. - So it comes off as a roguelike, then twists itself into being a puzzle game with low information given to the player, and very few tools to deal with the puzzle elements save drawing the perfect and and hoping the ai doesn't shoot your missiles off into the beyond. In the roguelike mode, the game attempts to balance itself by giving you a retreat function, this is a wholly unsatisfying way to play a roguelike, having to ram your head into a challenge, figure out it counters your deck in some way, then retreat, lose hp, retool your deck in the sense that you can "hide" 2 cards in reserves, the go back and attempt the challenge slightly more well suited hoping you don't draw badly. In other words, the game doesn't feel like it's underlining or celebrating your agency, it just kinda exists. sometimes you get the great satisfaction of some plan coming together, like being allowed to spam factories without the enemy attack waves overwhelming you. To only be faced with having to wait several turns for the enemy to spawn 1 ship at a time, and you basically just hitting end turn as fast as possible waiting for the battle to finish. It does have it's moments, it holds a buncha promsie where I'm drawn to the game in the hope I get to do some strategy, but overall it just failed to be exciting enough to really be worth the time.
Uber unique deckbuilding rpg, the story's cool, but the roguelike is where it's at
非常好游戏，像是回到了十五年前的夏天，打开小游戏网站，那种纯粹而枯燥的快乐 什么时候加入更多语言！拜托这个游戏真的超棒的！

A very fun and roguelike. The cards are fairly simple, kinda like MTG cards earlier in its lifespan. Which is something I like. But despite the simplicity of many of the cards, theres a good amount of strategy and fun synergies between the cards. Some questionable mission designs, like the ones that brutally punish structure based decks. Other archetypes dont have hard-counter missions like this so its odd that structures of all things are being treated like this. Dev also seems quite receptive to feedback, and makes frequent blog posts talking to the players. Also this dev is the same guy who made Keystone Card game in the SC2 arcade. so if you liked that game, you will definitely love this game. Just keep in mind that its a rogue like, and not a CCG like Keystone was.
I love the design, great game overall
An interesting mashup of genres. Rough around the edges, but worth playing.
Tax the colonies!!
building your deck up as you progress is very satisfying

The story mode was a nice surprise for me, It's the first time in awhile the characters felt well balanced and not forced. The gameplay is an enjoyable loop of autobattling/deckbuilding, however I will say that it is tricky to hyperfocus one strategy. Lots of stage challenges can mess up a deck, so making sure you can cover your bases is important. This leads to generally (in my experience) medium-large decks with rag tag good cards, but signature strategies (one of the boss/elite rewards) guarantee you have that card in your opening hand. The later stages of the Roguelike mode have been rough, but the dev is active and already added some perks to help out the early game, and is looking and adjusting things as of this review. The demo is very good, and you can see if you like the game play plenty with it. It's certainly worth a shot if you want a unique flavor of autobattler/card game.

This game is a lot better than i thought it would be. I played the demo and got hooked on it for a while, and decided to purchase it for the extra cards. I'm a huge fan of Auto-battlers, Rogue-like Deckbuilders, and just watching ships blow everybody up. I wish there were more cards, but i think the Dev is working on it. Campaign is a nice change of pace from constantly dying in the rogue-like mode. Give it a try if you are a fan of the genre.
